label: Hospital stay

what_happens.title: What happens at the hospital
goals: The steps: check in, a wristband, my own bed, nurses check, the doctors do their work, rest, go home
The hospital is a place where doctors and nurses help bodies get better
Each day has a plan, and the grown-up knows it
what_happens.parentSkill: Tell your child the plan you know in simple order, and say 'I don't know yet, we'll ask' when you don't.

who_is_there.title: Who is at the hospital
goals: Nurses, doctors and helpers wear name badges and introduce themselves
A grown-up from the family stays or visits, and says when
Other kids are in the hospital too
who_is_there.parentSkill: Say exactly who will be with your child and when, in words your child can repeat.

what_i_do.title: What I do at the hospital
goals: Wear the wristband, rest in the bed, tell a nurse how I feel
Use the call button to ask for help
Play, read and bring things from home
what_i_do.parentSkill: Practise telling feelings with words or a 1-to-5 hand: one finger is a little, five is a lot.

if_scared.title: If I feel scared at the hospital
goals: Beeps, bright lights, new smells and being in bed for a long time
Missing home and feeling worried are okay
Calm tools: a comfort toy from home, slow breaths, a hand to hold, a call or video
if_scared.parentSkill: Accept the worry and stay honest: answer only what you know, and promise only what you can keep.

rehearsal.title: Let's practise the hospital
goals: Pack a bag together: toy, pyjamas, a book, a photo
Play hospital with a toy in a pretend bed
Say the plan once more, ending with going home
rehearsal.parentSkill: Pack the hospital bag together and let your child choose what comes from home.

steps: Arrive at the hospital and check in at the desk
Get a wristband with my name on it
Go to a room with my own bed
Nurses check my temperature and listen to my heart
The doctors do their work to help my body
Rest, play, read and sleep in the hospital bed
Go home when the doctors say my body is ready
sensory: a bed that goes up and down with buttons
bright lights and a clean, soapy smell
a small clip on the finger that glows red
nurses who come in at night quietly
honestyNotes: Every hospital stay is different. Say only what you know about this stay, and use the hospital child life team where there is one. Some parts may hurt or feel uncomfortable; never promise it will not. Do not explain treatment or medicine; leave medical answers to the doctors and say "Let's ask the doctor".

questionButtons.text: Why do I go to the hospital?
fallbackAnswer: The hospital is where doctors and nurses help bodies get better.
The doctors will tell us more, and we can ask them anything.
[[GROWNUP]] will tell you exactly who stays with you and when.
Someone who loves you will be close, and the nurses are there all day and all night.
Some parts may feel uncomfortable or sore.
You can always tell a nurse, and helping you feel better is their job.
You go home when the doctors say your body is ready.
[[GROWNUP]] will tell you the plan each day.
Machines beep to tell the nurses how bodies are doing.
A beep is just a message for the nurse, and they come to check.
You sleep in a hospital bed with your own blanket and toy from home.
There is a button to call a nurse any time, even at night.
Nurses, doctors and helpers. They wear name badges and say their names.
You can ask anyone, what is your job?

questionButtons.text: Can I play at the hospital?
fallbackAnswer: Yes. Many hospitals have toys, books and a playroom.
You can bring your favourite things from home too.
[[GROWNUP]] and the doctors will tell you if you need an operation. If you do, you will know what happens before it starts.
You can ask the doctor any question, and they will answer it.
Sometimes nurses put in a tiny soft tube called a drip to give medicine or water. Putting it in can pinch, and then it mostly feels like nothing.
You can ask for numbing cream and hold [[GROWNUP]]'s hand.
Your teacher and friends will know you are getting better. Some hospitals even have a teacher who visits.
You can send a picture or a video to your class.

techniques.label: Bringing a comfort toy
techniques.how: Pack a favourite toy, blanket or pillowcase from home so the bed smells and feels familiar.

techniques.label: Packing the bag together
techniques.how: Let your child choose what goes in the hospital bag: pyjamas, a book, a toy, a family photo.

techniques.label: The 1-to-5 feelings hand
techniques.how: Practise showing how much something hurts or worries with fingers, one a little and five a lot.

techniques.label: Practising the call button
techniques.how: Find the call button together on the first day and practise pressing it once with the nurse.

techniques.label: A picture plan for each day
techniques.how: Draw the day in simple pictures (breakfast, check, rest, visit, sleep) and tick them off.

techniques.label: A video call with family
techniques.how: Plan a call with family or friends at a set time each day so there is something to look forward to.

techniques.label: Holding a hand
techniques.how: Hold your child's hand during checks and stay where your child can see you, when allowed.

techniques.label: Smell the flower, blow the candle
techniques.how: Breathe in slowly through the nose like smelling a flower and out like blowing a candle.

techniques.label: Asking for the child life team
techniques.how: Ask if the hospital has a child life specialist who can explain and play through what will happen.

ritual: Wristband on, bed and toy ready
Tell a nurse how I feel
Rest and get ready to go home

pain: Some parts may feel sore. Tell me or the nurse and we will help.
Show me on your hand: one finger a little, five a lot.
separation: Here is who will be with you, and when.
Your toy from home stays with you the whole time.
unknown: Here is today's plan. If I don't know, we'll ask the doctor.
You go home when the doctors say your body is ready.
strangers: The nurses and doctors wear name badges. Let's ask their names.
Their job is to help bodies get better.
sensory: The beeps are messages for the nurses.
The finger clip glows red. It just counts your heartbeat.
safety: You can press the call button any time, even at night.
The nurses are here all day and all night.
social: Other kids stay at the hospital too. Maybe there is a playroom.
We can call family on video tonight.
body: The doctors are helping your body get better.
You can always ask, what are you doing to my body?
love: I love you, every minute, even when I am not in the room.

sentences.text: Soon [[CHILD]] will stay at the hospital for a little while.
The hospital is a big building where doctors and nurses help bodies get better.
First, [[CHILD]] and [[GROWNUP]] check in at a desk.
Then [[CHILD]] gets a wristband with a name on it, like a special bracelet.
Before bed, [[GROWNUP]] tells [[CHILD]] an old story about a very tall bed.
Once upon a time, a princess travelled far from home.
One rainy evening, she came to a big castle and knocked on the door.
First, the helpers at the door said hello and wrote down her name.
Then they showed her to a room with a very tall bed.
The bed had many soft mattresses, one on top of another.
After that, the princess climbed into the tall bed to rest.
It was not her bed from home, and it felt strange.
A hospital stay is a bit like that.
There is a new bed, new helpers and a plan to help the body get better.
Tomorrow evening, the story goes on.
Next, [[CHILD]] goes to a room with a bed that moves up and down with buttons.
A nurse checks [[CHILD]]'s temperature and listens to the heart.
Then the doctors do their work, step by step.
After that comes resting, playing and sleeping, and at last, going home.
